title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sets up a coordinate-free normalization of the Legendre / level-2 picture for elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2.

**Möbius normalization.** Three distinct elements ξ1, ξ2, ξ3 ∈ k are given. These are the abscissae of the 2-torsion points of y² = (x−ξ1)(x−ξ2)(x−ξ3). The unique Möbius transformation with ξ1 ↦ 0, ξ2 ↦ 1, ξ3 ↦ ∞ sends the point ∞ to the parameter t. Concretely, φ(x) = (x−ξ1)(ξ2−ξ3) / ((x−ξ3)(ξ2−ξ1)), so t = φ(∞) = (ξ2−ξ3)/(ξ2−ξ1). This is the Legendre λ-invariant, i.e. a cross-ratio.

**Lines through the origin.** Grothendieck then passes to the linear picture. The points of P¹ are lines in k², and the figure shows the three lines through the origin spanned by the vectors (ξi, 1) on the affine line at height 1.

**The linear relation.** Three vectors in a 2-dimensional space satisfy a linear relation Σ λi (ξi, 1) = 0, i.e. Σλi = 0 and Σλiξi = 0. When the ξi are pairwise distinct, this relation is unique up to an invertible scalar. A canonical choice is λ1 = ξ2−ξ3, λ2 = ξ3−ξ1, λ3 = ξ1−ξ2. One checks Σλi = 0 and Σλiξi = 0 by direct expansion.

**Identification with the S3 representation.** Setting e_j − e_k := λi (ξi, 1) for (i, j, k) cyclic identifies k² with the sum-zero hyperplane of k³, i.e. the reduced permutation (A2 root) representation of S3. This sends the three marked lines of P¹ to the lines spanned by e2−e3, e3−e1, e1−e2. Equivalently, it is an S3 = GL2(F2)-equivariant identification of (P¹, three marked points) with the projectivized standard representation.

In this normalization t = −λ1/λ3, so the λ-invariant is a ratio of the canonical coefficients.

**Unfinished start.** The last lines begin a dual description: a linear form or basis f1, with (ξ1, 1) ↦ λ1 f1 + …, which is abandoned. The page serves the study of the level-2 moduli (the λ-line P¹ − {0, 1, ∞} with its S3 action) for modules of elliptic curves away from characteristic 2.
errors: No errors in what is written; the identities Σλi = 0 and Σλiξi = 0 for λi = ξj − ξk hold.
The final map (ξ1, 1) ↦ λ1 f1 + … is left incomplete.

ideas.what: Normalizing three distinct points of P¹ to 0, 1, ∞; the image of ∞ is the λ-invariant (cross-ratio).
ideas.modern_name: Legendre λ-invariant / cross-ratio; level-2 structure on elliptic curves

ideas.what: The unique linear relation among three vectors (ξi, 1) in k², with coefficients ξj − ξk, identifies k² with the A2 / reduced permutation representation, S3-equivariantly.
ideas.modern_name: Standard 2-dimensional representation of S3 ≅ GL2(F2); Vandermonde-type relations

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine classical computations (cross-ratio, linear relation among three vectors in a plane, S3-equivariant normalization) serving a level-2 setup. Nothing new for a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The arrow from ∞ points to t: the Möbius map sends ∞ to t; it is not a fourth point labelled separately.
Right of the bracket: 'Cela détermine (λi) mod mult. par scalaire inv.', with 'mult. par' added above the line; 'ξ1, ξ2, ξ3 deux à deux distincts' is the condition.
'or' is likely 'Or' or 'ou'; the word is uncertain.
In the figure the horizontal line at height 1 carries ξ1, ξ3, ξ2 in that order from left to right; a second horizontal line at height 0 passes through the origin.
